To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
generically the polynomial matrix set considered in this work is a set of minimal bases and that under perturbations these minimal bases are robust with smooth dual minimal bases.
the minimal bases with row degrees at most a given list of degrees are generically robust and their dual bases can be chosen smoothly.

, generically, polynomial matrices with bounded row degrees are minimal bases with right minimal indices equal to the sum of their row degrees, and under perturbations they remain minimal bases with their right minimal indices differing from this generic value at most by one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
generic and perturbation results in the linear space of polynomial matrices whose rows satisfy a given list of row degrees.
the following two main problems: (1) to characterize the minimal bases inside the considered linear space and (2) to study their perturbation properties.

the study of generic and perturbation results in a much more general linear setting than the one considered in [Van Doeren & Dopico, op. cit.] for polynomial matrices of degree at most $n$ (i.e., with all rows having the same degree $n$).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results in [Van Douren & Dopico, this http URL] are robust and can be extended to the case of polynomial matrices with row degrees bounded by an arbitrary given list.

the results proved in [Van Dooren & Dopico], which are valid for the case of polynomial matrices with degree bounded by a given natural number $d$, can be extended to a more general case in which the row degrees of the polynomial matrices are bounded by a list $d_ 1, \ldot s d_m$ of given natural numbers.

, generically, the considered set of polynomial matrices with bounded row degrees contains a smooth manifold of minimal bases with row degrees exactly equal, and with right minimal index sum equal to the sum of the row degrees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the considered sets of polynomial matrices with given row degrees, we have proved that the generic polynomial matrices are minimal bases and that, under perturbations of these matrices, the minimal bases can be robustly chosen and can be made to vary smoothly.

, in the case with given row degree bounds, the minimal bases and the minimal bases dual to them are robust under arbitrary perturbations and their properties are preserved by perturbations, as in the case with a common degree bound.

the results in this and in [Van Doeren & Dopico, op. cit.] are the polynomial matrix analogues of the results in [Van Doore, Dopico, & Lim, Linear Algebra Appl., 2017, this http URL], which were proved for the linear space of all $m\times n$ matrices of given rank.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the results in [Van Doeren & Dopico, 2016, Linear Algebra Appl., this http URL] on the generic and perturbation behavior of minimal bases of polynomial matrices of degree at most $n$ can be extended to a much more inhomogeneous setting.

, in contrast with the case of polynomial matrices with a common row degree, the generic minimal bases in this more general setting are not necessarily minimal bases of minimal size, and that the generic minimal bases of minimal sizes are not necessarily the minimal bases with their right minimal indices differing by one and with their sum equal to the sum of the row degrees.

, in the case with given row and column degrees, most of the classical theory of minimal bases and their perturbations can be generalized to a much more inhomogeneous setting, where the degree of each row can be chosen independently.
